verdict: Southwest set a third-quarter record with $8.4B of revenue, up 21%, and grew profit five-fold to $270M even though fuel costs jumped 62%.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; a Q3 record

segments.name: Passenger
segments.note: Ticket revenue from passengers — a third-quarter record, with the highest passenger yield in company history as bag fees and other commercial changes lapped their first year.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Cargo carried in the belly of passenger aircraft.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Loyalty program, fees and other revenue. The release prints $621M; shown as $620M so the three lines foot exactly to the $8,422M reported total after $1M of rounding.

opex.name: Salaries, wages & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for flight crews, ground staff and all other employees — the airline's biggest cost.

opex.name: Landing fees & airport rentals
opex.note: Fees to airports for gates, landings and terminal space.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of aircraft and equipment over their working lives.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: All other day-to-day operating costs, including $73M of special items. The release prints $1,026M; shown as $1,025M so expenses foot to the reported total after $1M of rounding.

takeaways.title: Record revenue, record yields
takeaways.text: Operating revenue was a Q3 record $8,422M and unit revenue rose 21.6% to an all-time record 18.55 cents per available seat mile, on strong demand for the revamped product.

takeaways.title: Fuel was the big headwind
takeaways.text: Aircraft fuel and related taxes cost $2,152M, up $821M or 62% from a year ago — yet operating margin still expanded 4.0 points to 4.5% because revenue grew faster.

takeaways.title: Clean profit was higher
takeaways.text: Excluding $73M of pre-tax special items, adjusted net income was $328M ($0.66 per share) versus the GAAP $270M ($0.55). Southwest also returned $176M to shareholders in dividends.

oneTimers: Special items cost $73M pre-tax in operating expenses ($58M after tax): excluding them, operating income was $452M instead of $379M and net income was $328M ($0.66 per share) instead of $270M ($0.55).
otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $24M: interest expense $70M, partly offset by $13M of capitalized interest, $33M of interest income and $1M of other gains, net.
footerNote: For an airline there is no printed gross-profit line; here aircraft fuel plays the role of cost of revenue and gross profit is revenue less fuel, exactly as the statement foots to $379M of operating income. Two lines differ by $1M from the printed release (other revenue and other operating expenses) so rounded millions foot exactly to reported totals — see the segment and expense notes.
